contents.name: Lemma 14.3
contents.support: Derivative identities specialized to Schwartz; Gaussian differentiation is justified directly by domination.

contents.name: Lemma 14.6, complex parameter extension
contents.reason: Complex-time Gaussian continuation exceeds the real positive summability parameter in this design; it is not used as an input.

contents.name: Corollary 14.14
contents.reason: General L2-by-L2 convolution into C0 is beyond the commissioned L1 convolution and Schwartz product inventory; no proof here uses this stronger extension.

contents.name: Theorem 14.16
contents.reason: The simultaneous compact-support impossibility theorem requires a separate support-uncertainty development; it is not the variance inequality requested here.

contents.name: Problem 14.2
contents.support: The density consequence is absorbed; intermediate Lp membership follows from boundedness and L1.

contents.name: Problem 14.3
contents.support: Tensor-product Fubini calculation used for the n-dimensional Gaussian.

contents.name: Problem 14.4, complex Poisson parameter
contents.reason: Only positive real Poisson kernels define the Abel approximate identities requested here; complex parameter continuation is not needed.

contents.name: Problem 14.6
contents.reason: The positive-transform alternative route to inversion is not used; Gaussian regularization supplies the design’s prescribed inversion proof.

contents.name: Problem 14.7
contents.reason: Non-surjectivity onto C0 is a separate range obstruction, stronger than the requested absence of a universal decay rate; neither result is being substituted for the other.

contents.name: Problem 14.8
contents.support: L2 comparison only; does not support the L1 theorem.

contents.name: Problem 14.9
contents.reason: Holomorphic strip extension from exponential decay belongs to complex Fourier analysis, outside these real-variable prerequisites.

contents.name: Problem 14.10, convolution of two measures
contents.reason: A complete measure-convolution algebra is outside the finite-measure uniqueness interface; Gaussian smoothing against a function is explicitly proved instead.

contents.name: Problem 14.11
contents.reason: Interval recovery with endpoint masses is a separate probability inversion formula; the design asks only finite-measure injectivity and normalization.

contents.name: Problem 14.12
contents.reason: Levy continuity and tightness concern weak convergence of probability measures, not the present uniqueness interface.

contents.name: Complex scalar conventions used in §14.1 (local interface expansion)
contents.support: The real-to-complex reduction is supplied as a local proof; not claimed as a separately numbered source theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 15.1 (three-lines)
contents.reason: The analytic interpolation input is owned by MT17 and is not reproduced in the Fourier prerequisites.

contents.name: Theorem 15.2 and Corollary 15.3 (endpoint interpolation)
contents.reason: MT17 owns Riesz–Thorin, but its published finite-target statement needs an endpoint extension before it can supply Hausdorff–Young. This is an open fatal interface finding, not a completed deferral.

contents.name: Corollary 15.4 (Hausdorff–Young)
contents.support: Orientation and endpoint comparison only. The intermediate-p conclusion is not proved or used in this batch.

contents.name: Following range and p>2 remarks
contents.reason: Fourier range classification and the p>2 obstruction require harmonic-analysis examples beyond the design’s interpolation orientation.

contents.name: Remark 11.8
contents.support: Moment domination is the differentiation input; no unwarranted differentiation of general L1 transforms.

contents.name: Proposition 11.9
contents.support: Bilinear transpose identity is a Fubini ingredient, not itself the sesquilinear Parseval assertion.

contents.name: Proposition 11.14, contour proof
contents.reason: The independent ODE-and-domination proof is used; contour shifting is an alternative proof rather than an additional omitted theorem.

contents.name: Remark 11.17
contents.reason: Plane-wave inversion is explicitly heuristic until tempered distributions are defined.

contents.name: Exercise 11.8(b)
contents.reason: Distribution-Schwartz convolution and its growth estimates require the next distribution pair.
